source.title: Minor interpretability exploration #1: Grokking of modular addition, subtraction, multiplication, for different activation functions

record.tranche_reason: The author says they redid modular-addition grokking with the original notebook/code, varying the arithmetic operation and activation function.
record.gate_note: The post reports qualitative outcomes for grokking timing and mechanistic features. It does not give numerical accuracy values in the text. The linked notebooks and plots are not present here. Optimizer experiments reported in the comments measure training-loss spikes and convergence, not delayed generalization itself.
record.test_reason: Reruns Nanda's modular-addition grokking notebook unchanged except for the operation (subtraction, multiplication), the activation function and LayerNorm. It reports, qualitatively, whether and when grokking happens and whether the Fourier algorithm is implemented.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The author concludes that subtraction uses the same Fourier clock algorithm as addition, that multiplication does not, that GELU greatly hastens grokking and SiLU only slightly, and that LayerNorm delays grokking without changing the algorithm. The record should add the LayerNorm finding and the author's framing of multiplication as a problem for universality needing further research.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the original grokking notebook/code, but changes the arithmetic operation and activation function and adds LayerNorm conditions.
record.method_sensitivity: Grokking timing varies with operation, activation function, and LayerNorm. Comment experiments report changes in spikes and convergence with learning-rate and optimizer choices.

fits_no_version.finding: Subtraction implements the same Fourier clock algorithm as addition, while multiplication shows a random-looking Fourier basis and no Fourier algorithm.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The modular-addition Fourier algorithm generalizes to related operations (subtraction) but not to multiplication. This is cross-task universality of the algorithm.

fits_no_version.finding: Learning-rate and optimizer changes alter training-loss spikes and convergence, with no delayed-generalization outcome reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Slingshot-like loss spikes in grokking runs depend on the AdamW learning rate.

record.problems: The post describes the exploration as small and low-stakes. The main text reports qualitative results without accuracy values, training-set sizes, uncertainty estimates, or detailed method settings. It points to external notebooks and plots that are not included in the text.

untested.parts: No accuracy values, chance or near-perfect levels, or training-set sizes are reported, and there is no test of whether the delay grows as the training set shrinks.
No continuous progress measure is tied to the test-accuracy jump, and removal of memorizing components is not measured directly.
Not tested: no non-algorithmic data and no initialization-scale or weight-norm manipulation.
Not tested: no large models or realistic data.
Not tested: no weight-decay variation, critical dataset size or ungrokking.
Different architectures beyond activation and LayerNorm swaps are not tested, and no quantitative algorithm-identification metric is given.

The comment experiments on learning rate and optimizer report loss spikes and convergence only. Whether delayed generalization disappears is not reported, and softmax floating-point effects are not tested.

missing.what: GELU gives tighter singular values, more neurons explained by the frequencies, and lower residual loss than ReLU, so the same Fourier algorithm is implemented more cleanly.
missing.locator: Results, Activation functions (GELU singular values and residual loss paragraphs)

missing.what: The author reran the experiments several times and reports results as 'very consistent'; this bears on seed noise and same-algorithm convergence.
missing.locator: Comments, author reply 'For 1 and 2 - I have.'

missing.what: SiLU lengthens the memorization phase while GELU does not.

record.verdict_notes: This is a single-author LessWrong post built on Nanda's notebook. All results are qualitative, with plots held externally. Nanda's work is an original source, but this post is not, so verdicts are allowed. The reader's V6 links for r5 were dropped because V6 concerns runs on the same task, not different operations. The optimizer rows in the comments do not report generalization timing, so they cannot bear on V7.

versions.untested_parts: The post does not state training-set sizes, chance or near-perfect test accuracy values, or whether the delay grows as the training set shrinks.
The post reports mechanistic features and their timing, but does not establish that memorizing components are removed later or that continuous progress measures anticipate the test-accuracy jump.
No non-algorithmic data, initialization-scale sweep, weight-norm intervention, or lazy-to-rich transition is tested.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data is studied.
The post does not test weight decay or another low-norm bias, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
The post varies activation functions, but does not report repeated runs, different architectures, or whether same-task runs converge to different algorithms.

The comments report optimizer changes affecting spikes and convergence, but do not measure whether controlling optimizer or numerical effects removes delayed generalization. Floating-point softmax limits are not tested.

rows.subject: Neel Nanda modular arithmetic network

rows.measure: Whether the learned algorithm is Fourier-based

rows.value: Subtraction uses the same Fourier algorithm.
rows.note: The post does not provide a numerical measure of algorithm identification.
rows.check: Subtraction using the Fourier algorithm is a cross-task universality result. It does not test gradual formation (V2) or same-task convergence (V6). Moved to fits_no_version.

rows.subject: Neel Nanda modular arithmetic network
rows.operation_detail: Examined the learned algorithm and Fourier basis for modular multiplication.
rows.measure: Whether the learned algorithm is Fourier-based
rows.value: The Fourier basis looks random and multiplication does not use a Fourier algorithm.
rows.note: The post also says ablating any frequency, including the same five used for addition, hurts multiplication performance; it does not give the size of that effect.
rows.check: Multiplication not using a Fourier algorithm is cross-task universality, not V2's gradual mechanism or V6's same-task claim. Moved to fits_no_version.
